title: Roster person
description: A named human who can approve things. Controls are owned by TEAMS (see control.schema.json owner) because person-owned controls die when the person leaves. But an approval is an ACT, and an act has a person behind it — so approved_by resolves here. This file exists to make 'who was entitled to approve that' answerable from the repo rather than from memory.

scope.description: What a person is entitled to approve. Tiering on risk.accept is by QUANTIFIED loss against the materiality threshold, not by H/M/L — this is the join between the CRQ output and who is allowed to sign.

grant.description: A scope held over a date range. Grants are dated because entitlement is a fact about a moment: an approval signed before the grant began, or after it ended, was not authorized — and that is only checkable if the range is on the record.

from.description: First date the grant is effective, inclusive.

until.description: Last date the grant is effective, inclusive. Absent = still held.

basis.description: Where the delegation comes from — a board resolution, a signed delegation of authority, an offer letter. Free text, but an empty basis is a delegation nobody can produce.

person_id.description: per.<slug>. Stable forever, never reused — approvals in already-issued artifacts point here.

teams.description: team_ids from roster/teams.yaml. Advisory: team membership does not confer authority, grants do.

is_principal.description: The fallback approver of last resort. Exactly one person should carry this. A program where the principal is the only approver for a scope is a program with an undelegated control — see G11.

departed_on.description: Last date employed. An approval dated after this is not valid however the grant reads.

authority.description: Dated scope grants. Empty means this person approves nothing.
